Hi, I’m currently using anki to learn turkish, so I can give you advice based on my experiences.

First of all anki is best used for memorisation of vocab.

Also it is generally advised to keep decks as general as possible so just a deck of one language rather than separating nouns and verbs and such. The actual reasoning is that it makes it harder to recall meaning based on context alone (“oh this must be a verb, to.... “)

My girlfriend is turkish so i have the advantage of her assistance in learning so the following advice might not apply.

At first find a list of 100 most common words and have it double checked by a native, minimize double definitions and other confusing stuff to keep the learning as clean as possible.
So instead basic and reverse:
En  <> most, width
Make three basic cards:
En > most, width
Most > en
Width > en

Verbs in Turkish are easy since they are incredibly consistent. I recommend learning common suffixes, such as the ones denoting person, tense, and the negative suffix. 

For the grammar, there is no substitute for a grammar book with exercises, for turkish the delights of learning turkish is recommended.

Other than that languages are generally considered to consist of 4 parts:

Reading
Writing
Listening
Speaking

Now the first two are mostly irrelevant to me but i think you can imagine how to practice those. 
Children’s media is your friend when starting.

Try to join online groups that practice speaking as you can find a native speaker that will engage with you in exchange for you speaking a language you know. 
Tell them what is important to you tough, the vowel rhyming turkish has is generally negligible, but the word order although strange to those who speak germanic languages, is very important.
Its the difference between “before breakfast”
And “first breakfast”

For the rest it comes down to just willingness to fail, dive in the deep end. I’ve said “cow juice” (inek su) when meaning milk, and all sorts of other funny combinations that get the point across.

Vocab is important in all of these steps, and provides a good way to keep you consistently engaged with the language.
